spec.name: customer-orders-portal
spec.type: Internal web app (customer & order directory) — release 1
spec.stack: Our usual web stack: Next.js (frontend) + NestJS (backend/API) running locally on this machine; PostgreSQL via Prisma for app data. Supabase (NEW to us) used specifically for two things only: (1) authentication and (2) file storage. NOT deployed — local only for this run.
spec.description: OBJECTIVE: Build a SMALL internal web app ('rep 1' = release/iteration 1) that lists our customers and, per customer, their orders. This is an internal tool (staff-only), not a public site. EXPLICIT OWNER CONSTRAINTS (verbatim intent, preserved): (a) use our USUAL web stack for the app itself; (b) authentication AND file storage MUST use Supabase — a platform we have NOT used before, so it must be connected and tested before build; (c) DO NOT deploy it yet — build and run locally only, no VM/Azure deploy in this run. PLATFORM: Next.js + NestJS (our standard web stack), PostgreSQL + Prisma for the app's own customer/order data; Supabase provides ONLY auth (login/session for internal users) and file storage (customer/order attachments). DATA SOURCE (assumption — stated so you can confirm): customers and orders are read from our already-connected systems — customers from HubSpot (CRM) and orders from Veeqo — synced into the app's Postgres for listing/drill-down; if you'd rather I seed a local DB instead of live-pulling for release 1, say so. FOLDERS: all work lives INSIDE the project's own folder workspace/projects/customer-orders-portal/ (frontend/ and backend/ subfolders) — nothing written at the Odin repo root. INTEGRATIONS: Supabase (auth + storage, to connect), HubSpot (customers, connected), Veeqo (orders, connected). DEPLOY: none this run — explicitly deferred per owner ('Do not deploy it yet'); no firewall/VM/rsync actions.
features: Authenticated login for internal staff via Supabase Auth (no public signup; internal users only)
Customers list view (searchable/sortable) sourced from HubSpot
Per-customer drill-down showing that customer's orders, sourced from Veeqo
Order detail view (line items, status, totals)
File storage via Supabase Storage — upload/view attachments against a customer or order
Sync layer pulling customers (HubSpot) and orders (Veeqo) into the app's Postgres
Runs locally only (dev server) — no deployment in this release

features.name: Role-based access (admin vs viewer)
features.why: Internal tool touching customer/order data usually needs at least a read-only vs admin split; cheap to add on top of Supabase Auth.

features.name: Audit log of who viewed/downloaded files
features.why: File storage of customer documents often has a compliance expectation; a simple access log is low effort now, painful to retrofit.

members.why: First time using Supabase for BOTH auth and file storage — a quick review of RLS policies, bucket permissions, and session handling prevents a misconfigured internal tool from leaking customer data. Not auto-staffed; approve to add.

members.name: Designer
members.why: Only if you want a polished internal UI; for release 1 Fullstack can use a standard component library, so left out by default.
